thesis_summary.thesis: Sable Offshore Corp. owns the Santa Ynez Unit, a cluster of federal offshore oil leases and three production platforms (Hondo, Harmony, Heritage) off the California coast, plus the onshore Santa Ynez Pipeline System that moves crude to market. **[Fact]** The company bought the field from Exxon Mobil in February 2024 and spent 2024–2025 restarting pipelines and platforms after years of shutdown. **[Fact]** First oil sales began March 29, 2026. **[Fact]** As of June 18, 2026, 52 of 77 completed wells were online at Harmony and Heritage, averaging about **43,000 gross barrels of oil per day** (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/424B5_20260630_rpt_acc0001628280_26_046144.htm`). **[Fact]** The field carries a **100% working interest with an 83.6% net revenue interest** (10-K), and its 2014 full-year peak was about **29,000 barrels of oil per day** gross. **[Fact]** The stock closed at **$3.08** on June 30, 2026, down about **56%** from $6.97 the prior day after the dilutive financing was announced.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: The market may be treating SOC either as a failed SPAC or as a normal E&P name, when it is actually a **dated capital-markets binary**: a cross-conditioned refinancing must close before the Exxon senior secured term loan matures July 24, 2026. **[Inference]** The 56% one-day drop to $3.08 shows the market repricing toward the diluted, leveraged reality. **[Inference]** Production is real (43k bbl/d) but that is likely elevated post-shut-in flush versus the 2014 peak of 29k bbl/d, so bears may overstate near-term default risk while bulls may overstate the sustainable production rate.
